Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Interim HUD note: pb-hud font fallback helps the current paragraph renderer and non-Latin EXIF/text values, but task #54 makes Description/Ask a rich panel with selectable/copyable text; the HUD is not the final rich-text surface. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images). || WWDC26 CONFIRMED (2026-07-04, https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/): FM image input is NEW in the 2026 release (macOS 27) — on-device, ships with the OS, no download/setup; API is session.respond { PROMPT; Attachment(x) } where x = NSImage/CGImage/CIImage/CVPixelBuffer/file-URL, any size/aspect. tasks.title: Vendor-patch wgpu-hal: presentsWithTransaction during window-mode transitions (flash-free resize, MTKView-grade)
tasks.description: Make the fullscreen-toggle / resize composite pixel-perfect on macOS. Today's mitigation (2026-07-04) is benign-not-atomic: layerContentsPlacement=.center + contentsGravity on the canvas view means the one racy composite ({new bounds, previous drawable} — wgpu presents out-of-band from the CA transaction that moves the bounds) shows UNSCALED stale content for <=1 frame instead of a stretch. The atomic fix is Apple's presentsWithTransaction (what MTKView flips on during live resize). wgpu-hal 22's Metal backend ALREADY implements the correct present branch (Surface.present_with_transaction pub field; present does commit -> wait_until_scheduled -> drawable.present(); the field's own doc comment cites resize-sensitive UI apps) — but wgpu 22 gives no safe way to SET it: Surface::as_hal hands out only a shared ref, there's no creation-time knob, and configure() re-asserts the flag onto the layer every resize (so flipping the CAMetalLayer property from Swift is useless). PLAN: (1) vendor wgpu-hal 22.0 with a ~20-line patch — interior-mutable flag (AtomicBool) + set_present_with_transaction(&self) — wired via [patch.crates-io] like the sevenz-rust2 precedent; (2) pb-render seam Renderer::set_present_with_transaction(bool) reaching the hal surface through Surface::as_hal; (3) flip it ON only around window-mode transitions (and optionally during live resize), OFF otherwise — presentsWithTransaction costs a main-thread waitUntilScheduled block per present, which MTKView itself only tolerates while resizing; the photo hot path (hold-to-blaze) never resizes, keypress->photon untouched; (4) owner drives the upstream PR against wgpu trunk — NOTE trunk's Metal backend was rewritten on objc2 in 23+, so the trunk patch is the same concept but different code; a hal-level setter is the least-bikesheddable API shape. When the eventual egui/wgpu upgrade train moves off 22, the vendored patch drops (if merged) or re-rolls. Payoff is polish: the remaining <=1-frame unscaled reveal on F-toggles/live-resize becomes zero-artifact.

Prior art: vertical-only *user*-resizing was PUNTED after 5 failed attempts (see git history + the comment above the TabView, and the ns2-native-dialogs memory); this is the different goal of auto-fit-to-content, not user-resize.
tasks.details: Approach to try (needs ON-DEVICE iteration — SwiftUI window sizing can't be verified headlessly): the Settings scene already uses .windowResizability(.contentSize), so per-tab fixed frames are what pin the size. Options: (a) drop the fixed heights and let contentSize follow each Form's natural height — historically the Forms expanded to fill instead of reporting intrinsic height, which is likely why it failed; (b) measure each pane's content height (onGeometryChange on the Form's content, guard against feedback loops) and apply it as the frame height; (c) keep fixed frames but compute them from the content once at build. Watch for: the object_setClass/KVO segfault hazard on SwiftUI windows (never do that); jumpy resize when switching tabs; the window collapsing to min. tasks.title: Cursor auto-hide option — hide the mouse pointer when idle / in speed mode (all platforms)
tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): let the mouse pointer hide, as an OPTION, on every platform where possible. Half the plumbing already exists but nothing actually hides today: contract::CursorKind::Hidden is defined (crates/pb-app-core/src/contract.rs:80) and its doc even claims 'the viewer hides the cursor in the chrome-free hot path and restores it on movement' — but (1) NOTHING in the core emits SetCursor(Hidden) (hover_cursor at app_core_impl.rs:2678-2686 only emits Grab/Grabbing/Pointer/Default), (2) the winit shell STUBS it: cursor_icon maps Hidden -> CursorIcon::Default (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs:3361, with the note 'Hidden is unused on the SetCursor path'), so Windows/Linux never hide, and (3) only the macOS shell honors it (CoreModel.swift:1897 NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true)) — and even that is dead code since the core never sends it. So this is: wire a core auto-hide POLICY, make the winit shell truly hide, confirm macOS, and expose it as a setting. 'Where possible': winit uses Window::set_cursor_visible(false) (works on Windows + X11; on Wayland cursor visibility is compositor-mediated and may be a soft no-op — accept graceful degradation there).
tasks.details: Design: (a) POLICY in core — after N seconds with no CursorMoved (and no panel/dialog/menu open, and pointer not over a clickable affordance), emit CoreEffect::SetCursor(CursorKind::Hidden); any real pointer movement restores the resolved cursor (Default/Grab/etc via the existing hover_cursor path). Drive the timeout off the existing tick-deadline machinery (next_deadline / self.now) — do NOT add a spin; the app already sleeps when idle, so schedule a wake at the hide deadline. A natural stronger default: in the borderless Fullscreen 'speed mode' (WindowMode::Fullscreen) hide sooner or immediately-on-idle, since that mode is the chrome-free hot path the contract doc references. (b) WINIT SHELL — replace the Hidden->Default stub: on SetCursor(Hidden) call window.set_cursor_visible(false); on any other kind restore visibility + set the icon. Track visibility so we don't thrash set_cursor_visible every event. Windows + X11 honor it; Wayland may ignore — that's the 'where possible' caveat, log/accept. (c) macOS — the core now actually emits Hidden; verify setHiddenUntilMouseMoves gives the desired feel, or switch to explicit NSCursor.hide()/unhide() (persistent hide with our own restore-on-move) if the until-mouse-moves auto-restore fights the policy. (d) SETTING — add a serde-default bool (e.g. settings.hide_cursor_when_idle, maybe an idle-seconds too) and surface a toggle in BOTH shells (egui Settings General/Appearance tab via a pb-ui toggle_with_label + the SwiftUI SettingsView), defaulting per owner (likely ON in fullscreen, or a simple global ON/OFF). Privacy #2: cursor state is ephemeral runtime state; the only persisted bit is the toggle in settings.toml — no viewing trace. Keep the policy pure/testable in pb-app-core (feed it 'now' + last-move time + mode + overlay state, assert it emits Hidden after the timeout and restores on move) so it isn't a shell-only behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: unit-test the idle policy in pb-app-core — given last-move time, now, window mode, and whether an overlay/affordance is active, assert it decides Hidden after the timeout and Restore on movement, and never hides while a dialog/menu/hover-affordance is up. Manual per platform: Windows (winit) — leave the pointer still over a photo, confirm it vanishes after the timeout and reappears on the first move; confirm it does NOT hide while hovering the Cancel-scan chip or with a panel/menu open; confirm it hides sooner/at-idle in fullscreen speed mode. macOS — same feel via the SwiftUI shell. Linux — X11 hides; note Wayland behavior. Settings: toggling the option OFF disables all hiding on every platform; the setting round-trips through settings.toml (and the SwiftUI FFI) and nothing else is persisted.

=== UPDATE 2026-07-14: #100 HAS LANDED. This is no longer conditional. ===
Windows now statically links THREE LGPL libraries, not two: libheif 1.23.0 + libde265 1.1.1 (LGPL-3.0-or-later, §4) and FFmpeg 8.1.2 (LGPL-2.1-or-later, §6 — vcpkg's own copyright file confirms LGPL-2.1; gpl/nonfree features are opt-in and off). FFmpeg's role on Windows is narrow (demux/metadata only; MF still does 100% of decode) but that is IRRELEVANT to the obligation — LGPL attaches to distribution and linkage, not to how much of the library is called. dav1d stays fine (BSD-2-Clause, attribution only, already handled).

A SHIPPED-DOC DEFECT was found and fixed while reviewing this (2026-07-14). THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is copied into the Velopack package by release-windows.ps1:158 — i.e. it ships next to the exe as the user-facing legal notice — and it stated "**Windows does not use FFmpeg** (Media Foundation handles video there)". .taskmaster/docs/ffmpeg-compliance.md said the same, and its entire argument rested on it. Both were true when written and were made false by #100. A Windows build cut in that window would have distributed FFmpeg under notices affirmatively denying it — materially worse than a documented open item. Both docs + CLAUDE.md's Licensing section now state the Windows static link and flag it. The underlying obligation is unchanged; only the honesty of the paperwork was restored.

THE DECISION (owner): DLL linkage vs static + published relink materials.
* DLL (LGPL-2.1 §6(b) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(1)) — the conventional answer, already what macOS and Linux do, so it makes all three platforms tell one story. Cost: vcpkg dynamic triplet (x64-windows / arm64-windows) instead of *-windows-static-md; ffmpeg-sys-next then wants VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 (the exact knob the `static` feature was added to defeat — see #100.1); build.rs changes; ~7 DLLs to stage, sign (Azure Trusted Signing) and ship per arch. NOT YET MEASURED: install size almost certainly grows — the +3.06 MB static figure exists because the linker discards every unreferenced object, and a DLL exports everything. That measurement should precede the call.
* Static + relink materials (LGPL-2.1 §6(a) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(0)) — legally recognized, and it keeps the small binary, but it requires publishing PhotoBlaze's OWN object files per release so a user can relink against a modified library. Object code, not source, so the proprietary position survives — but it is per-release, toolchain-specific plumbing that most vendors avoid for exactly that reason.
RECOMMENDATION: DLL. Measure the size delta first so the call is made on numbers.

=== MEASURED 2026-07-14 — the size objection to DLLs is DEAD (+0.8 MB). ===
Built the whole native stack against vcpkg's DYNAMIC x64-windows triplet (libheif[core], dav1d, ffmpeg with the SAME demux-only portfile trim) and compared like for like:
  STATIC  (ships today): exe 35.07 MB                       = 35.07 MB
  DYNAMIC (LGPL remedy): exe 29.04 MB + 7 DLLs 6.82 MB      = 35.87 MB
  DELTA: +0.80 MB (+2.3%) on-disk payload.
The going-in fear was a 10-15 MB regression, reasoning that a DLL exports everything while a static link lets the linker discard unreferenced objects. That reasoning was WRONG at this scale: the exe shrank 6.03 MB and the DLLs only weigh 6.82 MB back. Do not re-litigate this from intuition.

The DLLs (transitive closure of the real import table via dumpbin, not a guess): avcodec-62 1.94, dav1d 1.70, heif 1.33, avutil 0.84, avformat 0.54, libde265 0.35, swresample-6 0.12. NOTE swscale-9.dll is NOT needed — Windows only reads containers, so the scaler is never imported. VERIFIED RUNNING: photoblaze.exe copied to an empty dir with exactly those 7 DLLs starts and reports its version, so the set is complete (nothing is dlopen'd behind dumpbin's back — libheif's plugin loader is already OFF via the portfile patch).

HOW IT WAS BUILT (the seam is committed and inert by default):
* pb-decode/build.rs takes PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 -> the plain x64-windows / arm64-windows triplet and dylib= link kinds. Unset = today's static behaviour, byte for byte.
* FFmpeg additionally needs VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 in the env. It does NOT need the ffmpeg-next 'static' feature removed: ffmpeg-sys-next only SETS that var when 'static' is off (build.rs:700-706) and never unsets it, so an externally-set value survives and the vcpkg crate honours it. That is why the whole spike flips on two env vars with no Cargo.toml edit — worth knowing, since #100.1 added 'static' specifically to defeat that variable.

STILL TO DO for a real DLL ship (none of it measured yet): setup-libheif.ps1 installs the dynamic triplet; release-windows.ps1 stages the 7 DLLs into $Stage and signs them (Azure Trusted Signing) alongside the exe; CI lanes; arm64. dav1d is BSD-2 so it could stay static, but one triplet supplies the tree — splitting it buys ~1.7 MB of DLL for extra build complexity, probably not worth it.

=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-14: Windows now links the LGPL libraries as DLLs by default. ===
The three obligations turned out to be INDEPENDENT, and all three are now addressed:
  1. LINKAGE (LGPL-2.1 6(b) / LGPL-3.0 4(d)(1)) - the default flipped to DLLs. build.rs
     `vcpkg_dynamic()` is now dynamic-by-default with `PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1` as the A/B escape
     hatch (the spike's polarity was the reverse: PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 opted IN). A
     PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1 build is the non-compliant configuration by definition and must never ship.
  2. LICENSE TEXT (LGPL-2.1 6 / LGPL-3.0 4(b)) - `licenses/` ships verbatim COPYING files for
     libheif, libde265, FFmpeg (LGPLv2.1) and dav1d, staged into the Velopack package, the macOS
     .app (Contents/Resources/licenses) and the AppImage (usr/share/licenses). This was MISSING ON
     EVERY PLATFORM and was the most exposed item: unlike the static link (which had 6(a) as a
     fallback defence), shipping without the licence text has no defence at all.
  3. ATTRIBUTION (LGPL-3.0 4(c)) - triggered only because About displays a copyright line; the
     About card now names each bundled library + its copyright and points at the licences folder.

FFmpeg follows the switch WITHOUT an env var: pb-decode's `ffmpeg-next` dep no longer enables the
`static` feature, and ffmpeg-sys-next sets VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 itself exactly when `static` is absent.
Re-adding `features = ["static"]` there silently returns FFmpeg to a non-compliant static link -
Cargo.toml carries a warning comment saying so.

TWO TRAPS FOUND WHILE WIRING IT (both cost real time, both now handled + documented):
* libde265's import lib is `de265.lib` but its static lib is `libde265.lib` - the vcpkg triplets
  disagree on that ONE name (heif.lib and dav1d.lib are stable across both, and the DLL is still
  libde265.dll). A `dylib=libde265` link name gives LNK1181. The link name must track the triplet,
  not just the link kind.
* `Enter-VsDevShell` OVERWRITES VCPKG_ROOT with the vcpkg bundled inside Visual Studio - a tree with
  none of our pinned ports - even when the caller exported the right value first. Since ffprobe
  needs a Developer shell (bindgen), EVERY shipped build passes through this. scripts/vs-dev-env.ps1
  now captures VCPKG_ROOT and restores it (falling back to ~/vcpkg like build.rs does, because
  ffmpeg-sys-next has no such fallback and would otherwise hunt for FFmpeg in the VS tree).

Also: build.rs copies the vcpkg DLLs into target/<profile>/ AND target/<profile>/deps/ (Windows
resolves from the executable's own directory, and cargo puts tests in deps/), so `cargo run`/`cargo
test` work with no PATH dance and the shipped DLL set is the one the tests ran against.

REMAINING before this can be closed:
* ARM64 is UNVERIFIED end to end (no ARM64 box) - the dynamic triplet, the de265.lib naming and the

* No release has actually been cut with the DLL config yet; release-windows.ps1 stages the DLLs via a

* The `cargo license` sweep of the rest of the dependency tree (per this task's details) is still not

subtasks.title: macOS fill latency: poster tiles retained + no double walk (owner-measured)
subtasks.description: Owner on \\beenas.local\Media\Videos: opening the strip on a movie folder showed blank placeholders for NEARLY A MINUTE. ROOT CAUSE = starvation, not throughput: the pool's documented order is 'every display/poster want ahead of every thumb want' (decode_pool.rs:22), so thumb fills cannot start until the whole display prefetch window drains, and on a movie folder every one of those is a multi-second network walk. TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES tried first, recorded so they are not re-derived: (a) 'raise the thumb concurrency cap' - wrong layer, a concurrency limit trickles tiles from second one rather than withholding them for a minute; (b) 'the #114 selection dedup is the cure' - it halves work per VISITED movie but does not reduce N distinct movies x one walk each. FIXES: (1) 6b701b3b - thumbs_capture retains a VIDEO's displayed image as its tile even when the strip was never opened (a video's displayed image IS its poster, already paid for); photos keep the `enabled` gate because a photo thumb is a cheap local re-decode and capturing every displayed photo would put a derive on every frame of a blaze. TRAP: gating on `capture` instead of turning it ON is a NO-OP off Windows - enable_capture()'s only call site is land_selection_tile, which is cfg!(windows). (2) the double-walk fix - every film in the display window was walked TWICE concurrently (Display poster + Thumb fill), because the only guard (pending_items) is built from pending_uploads i.e. decodes that already RETURNED, so an in-flight walk was invisible; suppression is scoped to !poster_select_supported() so the Windows selection branch keeps its Demand::Thumb union (which routes a FAILED walk into thumbs.failed). MEASURED (owner, PB_THUMB_DIAG=1, same share): first tile 199 ms (from ~60 s), 10 tiles <1 s, 70 tiles in 17 s. Remaining: a ~700 ms/tile plateau from ~1 s to ~15 s = fill walks contending with the still-draining display window; ONLY the #114 selection parity would collapse that (worth ~10-14 s on that folder), deliberately not scheduled.

tasks.title: Fill scale mode: cover-to-screen decode target (semantic Contain/Cover)
tasks.description: Task #18 finding #2. decode_fit() returns None for ScaleMode::Fill, so a 24MP HEIC in Fill decodes/uploads at full res though only a screen-sized cover crop shows. Fix with a SEMANTIC decode target (Contain vs Cover) computed per-image after each decoder knows its oriented dimensions - NOT a single current-dims cover box in decode_fit (that mis-sizes neighbors: a portrait neighbor of a landscape current gets 2x-upscaled and it sticks once resident).
tasks.details: Owner decision (2026-07-14): use the semantic Contain/Cover target despite ~40 FitBox construction sites across 3 crates - a mechanical change, preferable to shipping a known sharpness regression. downscale_to_fit currently uses min() (contain); Cover uses max(sw/w, sh/h) clamped to no-upscale, computed against each image's own dims, so the box can stay image-independent (the screen box) and neighbors are correct too. AUDIT ALL 9 decode_fit() consumers (not just prefetch + slot_bytes_estimate): it also drives video scaling/budgeting, animation decoding, Live Photo streaming, and macOS archive posters. Benefit for HEIC is upload/VRAM/CPU-downscale (finalize applies the box after a full decode), not decode time.

tasks.title: Performance: fast archive opens, instant resize, instant thumbnails
tasks.description: Measured baseline (2026-07-17, PB_PERF on an SMB album.zip of 8 ~36MP JPEGs): open->first-photo 7068ms, open->all-cached 8302ms, resize Fit<->1:1 711-993ms. The first photo is ~85% of the whole open (all 7 remaining cache in +1.2s), so metric 1 is a large SERIAL/fixed cost, not per-photo throughput. Instrumentation lives in pb_app_core::perf (PB_PERF env; folded into --metrics). Prime directive: the app must FEEL fast.

subtasks.title: Encoded-byte cache in front of source.bytes()
subtasks.description: Every image decode calls source.bytes(item) (engine.rs:512), which for a ZIP re-inflates/re-reads the entry every call - so a resize (epoch bump -> re-decode) re-reads 39MB off SMB (~0.8s measured). Add a small bounded RAM-only LRU of encoded (inflated) bytes, consulted before source.bytes(). Kills the re-read for resize, preview->full upgrade, revisit, OCR, Describe. Highest value on archives/SMB (expensive bytes()), near-free on FsSource (OS page cache). RAM-only, dropped on nav/Esc (privacy #2, same category as pending_uploads). Decide scope (archive-only vs all) + byte budget. Behind a seam + A/B via PB_PERF resize numbers.

subtasks.title: Break down the 7s open->first-photo (it is NOT a full unzip)
subtasks.description: CORRECTION: a ZIP is already lazy - open reads only the central directory + a local header per entry (ZipSource::open), then bytes(i) inflates ONE entry on demand. It is 7z that is eager (whole archive -> RAM on open, because solid). So the 7s is NOT unzip-everything; it is ~all the 39MB single-entry read over SMB + ~0.3s decode. Sub-instrument metric 1 into phases (open-cmd -> worker/central-dir done -> first bytes() read -> first decode -> present) to confirm the read dominates. NB a ZIP is not background_open (kind.rs:50) so open runs sync on the event loop; verify that is not itself a stall.

subtasks.title: Thumbnails: keep a tiny window warm when parked (bounded, off by default cost)
subtasks.description: Owner call: do NOT always-capture everything (thumbs are off by default; bad trade for never-users). Happy medium: keep capture off by default, but when PARKED (held_nav is none), derive thumbs for a tiny window - current + next 2-3 - off-thread on the existing derive thread. Those items are already decoded/resident, so it is pure downsample (tens of ms each), zero source reads. Result: opening the panel always shows the neighbors instantly + rest fill on scroll, instead of a wall of placeholders for seconds. Blaze pays nothing (parked-gate); RAM capped (handful). Today thumbs_capture (app_core_impl.rs:2160) is gated on thumbs.enabled which only flips on first panel open (thumbs.rs:107), so a browse-then-open re-reads all N from SMB via Job::thumb. The ring-reuse (GPU-downsample a resident VRAM texture) stays a fallback for evicted items.

subtasks.title: First-image priority / bandwidth on a slow source
subtasks.description: The prefetch already ranks the on-screen photo tier-1 (request_prefetch sharpen/head), but on a slow source its full-res read competes for bandwidth with the whole window's preview reads. Explore throttling concurrent reads from an archive/slow source so the first image isn't fighting its neighbors. Separable from the byte cache; only pursue if #2 shows read-bandwidth contention (vs a fixed open cost).

subtasks.title: Preview-first for big JPEGs via the embedded EXIF thumbnail
subtasks.description: The real fix for the 7s first-photo over SMB. Large JPEGs embed a small thumbnail near the file start (owner test file: JPEGInterchangeFormat 240, len 22467 = 22KB). We already have pb_decode::exif_thumbnail but only use it for the thumbs strip; the main viewer decodes the full JPEG and shows nothing until done. Read just the first ~128KB of the entry, pull the embedded thumb, show it in ~100ms (blurry, fit-to-screen), then read the full entry in the background and upgrade to sharp (the preview-first model RAW/HEIC already use). Needs (a) a partial entry read - bytes() reads the whole entry today; (b) a JPEG preview-first path in decode. Turns 7s of placeholder into instant-preview->sharpen.

subtasks.title: Resize: jump to true 1:1 SIZE instantly (upscale the fit texture), then sharpen
subtasks.description: Owner-observed two-stage Fit->1:1: (1) a small grow to an intermediate size, (2) ~1s spinner, (3) a jump to true pixel-1:1. Cause: in Fit mode finalize (common.rs:84) downscales the texture to the fit box (true res kept only as orig_width/orig_height), and ViewTransform base_scale for Original is 1.0 = draw the bound texture at 1:1 of ITS dims (view.rs:110). So the toggle shows the low-res fit texture at 1:1-of-reduced-dims (near fit size, wrong) until the full-res re-decode lands and present_slot re-places at the true dims (the big jump). Fix: on the toggle, place the quad at the TRUE size using orig_width/orig_height and let the GPU upscale the fit texture - so you jump to the correct SIZE instantly (soft), then only sharpness improves when the full decode arrives. One soft->sharp transition, no intermediate size step. The resize twin of #106.5 (EXIF preview-first); pairs with #106.1 (byte cache) so the sharpen is not gated on an SMB re-read.

subtasks.title: Hold the full-res of the PARKED photo so 1:1/zoom is instant (the real zoom win)
subtasks.description:
MEASUREMENT (warm, PB_PERF): reads are ~37ms/33-38MB (OS SMB cache warm - the 7s first-photo was the ONE-TIME cold read); steady-state the DECODE (~300-500ms per 36MP JPEG) is the whole cost. Every Fit<->1:1 toggle bumps the geometry epoch and re-decodes the WHOLE ring at the new fit (log: items 0-7 re-decode around each resize). Root cause (owner, confirmed): decode-to-fit only caches the fit-sized texture and discards the full-res (true res kept only as orig_width/orig_height, common.rs:84), so 1:1 re-decodes every time - even toggling back and forth.

DESIGN (owner, 2026-07-17): while BLAZING keep decode-to-fit (small, the prime directive). When PARKED, background-decode + HOLD the full-res for a small SEQUENTIAL window - current + previous + next (radius 1, 3 items) by default; NOT the random-deck neighbors. Then Fit<->1:1<->Fit on the current photo (and on an immediate neighbor after one nav) are instant REBINDS - decode paid once, in the background, never on the toggle. Serve BOTH modes from the full-res (GPU downscales for Fit, 1:1 for Original). Drop full-res outside the window on nav.

CONFIGURABLE + OOM-SAFE (owner: easy to dial in; constrained systems must be able to reduce it): a Settings knob for the full-res cache radius - 0 = current only (or off), 1 = current+/-1 (default), maybe up to a small cap. VRAM math: 36MP RGBA8 ~= 144MB each, so radius 1 = ~432MB of full-res on top of the fit ring; bound it against a VRAM budget and let a slow box dial to 0. Random-deck neighbors are a possible later addition (owner may want after real use), left out for now. REPRIORITIZES: #106.1 byte-cache is a COLD/SMB win (nothing for a warm resize); THIS is the actual zoom win.

tasks.title: Copy: one honest "Copy" that copies whatever makes sense (pixels and/or the file)
tasks.description: Owner's insight 2026-07-17: "on the mac, don't you kind of get both?" Both platforms' clipboards are multi-representation, so offer every representation that makes sense and let the TARGET pick - Photoshop takes the pixels, Explorer takes the file. *** SCOPE WARNING: most of this is ALREADY BUILT - verify before planning. *** (1) The two-format copy SHIPS: clipboard.rs's module doc already argues this rationale; Windows writes CF_DIBV5 + CF_HDROP together (win::set takes path: Option<&Path>), macOS writes .tiff + .fileURL on one NSPasteboardItem (CoreModel.swift:3216). (2) The label is half-converged: macOS's menu bar ALREADY says "Copy" (MenuBar.swift:293); only menu.rs:1269 (Windows) and CoreModel.swift:1111 (the macOS context menu) still say "Copy Image". (3) A door ALREADY copies its file - source.path(item) is a real path, so CF_HDROP is already offered and you can paste an archive into Explorer today. REAL REMAINING WORK: (a) relabel "Copy Image" -> "Copy" in the two places above; (b) don't offer an image when there isn't one - on a door, skip the decode and emit a ClipboardPayload::File { path } arm (Windows drops the DIB from win::set; macOS's `if let tiff` is already conditional so it just skips); (c) LINUX WRINKLE: arboard has no file-list support, so set_image_and_file there already ignores the path and copies pixels only - a file-only payload would land NOTHING, so fall back to the path as text. WHY ONE GENERIC LABEL: muda has no menuNeedsUpdate, so per-item relabelling means a menu rebuild per item ON THE BLAZE PATH (the rebuild-on-signature pattern used by the subtitle flyout). "Copy" needs no rebuild and is never a lie. NON-GOAL (owner, 2026-07-17): a Copy Filename command. Copy File Path copies the full path and the owner says that's the main use case and the more useful of the two. Separate commit from #105 (touches both shells, improves photos too), but it's an afternoon.

tasks.title: Harden the deck-open pipeline against cross-type races (deferred follow-ups)
tasks.description:
Follow-ups from the Codex root-cause review of the 'archive door card frozen over a photo' bug (fixed 2026-07-17 by a core-side extend guard in apply_scan_batch + a winit shell cross-cancel of the folder-scan and archive-open workers). The primary bug (mode A: a stale folder-scan batch extending an archive deck) is fixed on BOTH shells by the core guard. These are the remaining, lower-severity hardening items Codex recommended:
(1) macOS shell (pb-mac-ffi) parity: mirror the winit begin_archive_open/begin_dir_scan cross-cancel so starting either worker drops the other. Without it, macOS is still exposed to 'mode B' (a stale folder scan's FIRST batch bootstrapping over an archive opened just after the scan started) - LOW severity (a clean rebuild onto the wrong-but-valid folder deck, not the frozen-view corruption; the core guard already covers mode A on mac). Needs an on-device build to verify (cfg(macos), can't compile on Windows).
(2) Shared open generation (Codex #1/#2): replace the global scan_bootstrapped boolean + independent archive_gen/scan_gen with ONE monotonic open generation shared by both worker types, threaded through the contract (BeginArchiveOpen/BeginDirScan effects + ArchiveResolved/ScanBatch events carry it), so any result whose generation != the latest open is dropped in the core - the general, race-proof fix that also closes mode B shell-neutrally.
(3) DONE 2026-07-19 via task #119 - Decode identity (Codex #4): DecodeKey carries content_gen on every job (dedup identity included); staleness is per-validity-domain (decode_pool::validity) at the pool cancel, ingestion, rebuild retention, and drain gates. Cross-deck decodes can no longer dedup as current. See plans/119-decode-validity-domains.md.
(4) DONE 2026-07-19 - Renderer upload correctness (Codex #5): Renderer::upload_slot now returns bool (false + loud stderr on an out-of-bounds slot, gpu.rs); both drain_results call sites gate on it - the reserve path rolls the reservation back (release_pending) and the upgrade path keeps preview_resident/sharpen bookkeeping untouched; both production mark_resident returns (the reserve path and the GPU-derive path; the upgrade path has none) are checked with a loud [ring-desync] error instead of ignored. Regression tests: a_refused_upload_is_never_marked_resident_and_rolls_back + a_refused_upgrade_upload_keeps_the_preview_sharpen_eligible (a RefusingUploads Renderer double; pb-render now re-exports wgpu so doubles can name device/queue types).
(5) present_item result propagation (Codex #6): make present_item return success and have try_present_target/drain_results propagate it; on a genuine present_slot miss, abort the current drain batch and resync ONCE after the loop (never invalidate mid-loop - that was the reverted cff70ca0/c383107a repair that bumped the epoch mid drain_results and purged the retained full-res tier, regressing instant fullscreen to a preview flash).
Codex full analysis saved during the 2026-07-17 session. tasks.title: Parked instant-quality: fullscreen toggles kill the viewport-independent Original decode (blurry toggle storm + blurry advance)
tasks.description:
OWNER-VERIFIED + CLOSED 2026-07-19 (engagement-shoot smoke): toggle-storm gone, no re-decode on toggle; residual blur only when moving fast+aggressively past the banked window on high-res photos - the designed decode-throughput envelope (levers if ever wanted: full_res_radius, #112 profiles).
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-19 (plan: .taskmaster/plans/119-decode-validity-domains.md, rev 3; three Codex rounds folded - two plan, one implementation-diff with 3 bug fixes incl. the mac poster-straggler request_id fence): Validity domains (Geometry|Content) declared per work kind in decode_pool::validity (exhaustive match), DecodeKey carries content_gen (retires the PosterSelect epoch smuggling + Want::sel_gen), enforced at FOUR gates - pool cancel arms (epoch change kills Geometry only; content change kills all; empty want-set quiesces), ingestion (absorb_results/drain try_recv), rebuild_ring retention (retain by predicate instead of clear), drain admit (before purpose routing). Plus: invalidate_content quiesces the pool + advances the thumbs fence (view-state preserving, generation-keyed pending), work_pending covers pool.has_work() (outstanding-outcome counter over the send/untrack handoff) + staged uploads, cross-deck dedup hole (#109.3) closed. 13 new tests (6 pool, 5 core, 2 thumbs); workspace green. REMAINING: owner manual verify - the engagement-shoot repro with PB_SHARP_DIAG=1; expect at most ONE blurry toggle ever (the '[sharp-diag] cross-epoch ... admitted' line = the fix firing), and a sharp advance after settling.
Owner repro 2026-07-19 (D:\Media\Pictures\2022\2022-06-20 - Don Epp Engagement Shoot): blaze past the buffer, park (sharpens in ~0.5s), hit F -> blurry then clears; toggle F repeatedly -> blurry EVERY time for 4-5 toggles, then suddenly every toggle is instant; advance to the next photo -> blurry again. The #110/#106.7 machinery is supposed to make all of this a rebind/derive.
ROOT CAUSE (verified in source 2026-07-19, not yet live-confirmed): a fullscreen toggle bumps the geometry epoch, and BOTH pipeline gates treat epoch as universal staleness:
(a) DecodePool::set_targets cancels every queued/in-flight job except Purpose::PosterSelect on an epoch change (decode_pool.rs ~539-557) - including RepKind::Original decodes, which are viewport-independent (native size, no fit box);
(b) drain_results drops ANY outcome whose o.key.epoch != self.epoch ('stale geometry', app_core_impl.rs ~7612) - an Original that finishes decoding mid-toggle is discarded on landing.
So the parked full-res Original (#106.7 tier, queued below thumbs) restarts from ZERO on every toggle. Until the user pauses long enough for it to land, each toggle is a full CPU Fit re-decode with a stretched held-frame interim (= the blur). Once the Original finally survives to residency, item-6 retain/remap + resize_hold + GPU derive make every later toggle instant - exactly the observed 'suddenly consistently clear after 4-5 tries'. The blurry advance is the same failure: every toggle also killed the neighbours' Fit refills AND their parked Originals, so derive-on-nav has no source and the advance falls back to preview-first.
FIX (the #114 PosterSelect exemption is the in-tree template - 'a resize must not kill a multi-second walk whose choice is viewport-independent'; the same argument holds verbatim for Originals):
(1) set_targets: RepKind::Original display jobs survive an epoch change (still cancelled when no longer wanted, and on content changes).
(2) drain_results: staleness for Original outcomes is CONTENT identity, not geometry epoch. Do it properly via #109 item 3: add content_gen to DecodeKey and its dedup identity; Fit staleness = epoch AND content_gen, Original staleness = content_gen only. This lands the tech-debt audit finding-#3 'epoch carries geometry identity but not deck identity' item at the same time and retires the PosterSelect epoch-smuggling hack's uniqueness.
(3) Confirm live with PB_SHARP_DIAG + PB_PERF: rapid F toggling never restarts the Original decode; the first toggle after Original residency has NO blur phase; advance-after-settle GPU-derives sharp when the neighbour's Original is resident.
ACCEPTANCE: unit tests - an Original outcome landing with an older key.epoch but current content_gen is admitted and marked resident; a cross-deck Original (stale content_gen) is dropped; a stale-epoch Fit outcome is still dropped. Owner re-runs the engagement-shoot repro: at most ONE blurry toggle (the one racing the very first Original decode), then instant; advance after settling is sharp.
While in there: sanity-check GPU-derive eligibility on this corpus (derive_fit refuses mode-1 ICC / clamped sources) - if these JPEGs are mode-1, post-residency toggles lean on resize_hold + the held frame instead, which must still present sharp (no preview flash). Relates: #109(3), #110; the diagnostics panel (#120) would have made this visible immediately.

tasks.title: #119 follow-ups: derive-before-preview on nav + the repeated cross-epoch Original admit loop
tasks.description:
OWNER-VERIFIED + CLOSED 2026-07-19 (same smoke as #119): blur now occasional and provoked (fast+aggressive+high-res past the banked window), not systematic.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-19. Item 2: ResidentRing gained a 'denied' refusal latch (recorded on genuine reserve_bytes refusals; cleared by clear/compact_to/set_displayed CHANGE - nav/rebuild re-ranks the keep list) plus a pure admittable() dry-run mirroring the reserve rules; the parked-tier emitter skips denied items and pre-flights Original wants via admittable with a meta-based mip-chain estimate (unknown meta passes; the latch is the airtight backstop). A sharp-diag line logs parked refusals. Item 1: try_gpu_sharpen moved OUTSIDE the tick's held-key gate with its own blaze_repeating gate (held AND past initial_delay; the ADR-024 watchdog overrides) - a tap's advance GPU-sharpens with the key still down; sharpen_now (the CPU decode want) keeps its key-up gate unchanged. Tests: 4 pb-core (admittable/reserve mirror, latch lifecycle), 4 core (the livelock pin via a cfg(test) pool enqueue log, pre-flight negative+positive, tap-window sharpen, blaze-repeat defer). NOTE: a Codex diff round was attempted but the CLI hit its usage limit (resets Jul 24) - self-reviewed against the planned risk list instead. Owner verify with PB_SHARP_DIAG=1: expect 'ring refused parked ... denied until rebuild/nav' AT MOST ONCE per item per park (not 30x), and no preview flash on a tap-advance when the Original is resident.
Two findings from the owner's first #119 verify log (2026-07-19, PB_SHARP_DIAG=1; the fix itself is confirmed working - cross-epoch admits + GPU derives/sharpens firing, no re-decode on toggle):
(1) Advance-after-toggle still flashes the preview even when the neighbour's Original IS resident. try_gpu_derive_fit fires only on a total nav MISS (no Fit resident at all); a resident PREVIEW counts as presentable, wins the keypress, and the derive sharpens a beat later ('parked on item=8 as a resident PREVIEW' -> 'GPU-sharpened item=8'). Refinement: on nav, when the target's resident Fit is a preview AND a derive-eligible (mipped, non-clamped, non-mode-1) Original is resident, GPU-derive the exact Fit and present THAT instead of the preview - the derive is a GPU dispatch (rebind-class cost), so this stays within the never-CPU-decode-on-keypress rule. This closes the owner's remaining 'next image comes up blurry after f,f' gap.
(2) INVESTIGATE: one item's Original was admitted ~30 times in a short window ('cross-epoch Original admitted item=7' x ~30) - each line is a separate COMPLETED native decode of the same photo. Suspected shape: parked tier wants item 7's Original -> decode lands -> reserve_bytes refuses (item_rank >= ring capacity, or byte budget with nothing lower-priority evictable) -> outcome consumed (never resident, never failed) -> pending_reps empties -> next prefetch pass re-requests -> loop. Burns a full native decode per prefetch pass, competing with the very refills the user is waiting on. Structurally predates #119 (a budget-refused Original could always loop) but #119 made it visible/reachable cross-epoch. Fix sketch: on a reserve refusal for a parked-tier rep, remember (item, rep, epoch/content_gen) in a small denial set consulted by the parked-tier emitter until targets/geometry change - or make full_res_window/eligibility agree with reserve_bytes' rank-vs-capacity rule so the want is never emitted for an item the ring will refuse. Add a PB_SHARP_DIAG line on the refusal path first to confirm the mechanism before fixing.

tasks.title: Instant F-toggle before the Original lands: current-Original priority + a geometry-pair Fit stash
tasks.description:
FIX 2 SHIPPED 2026-07-19 (plan: plans/123-geometry-pair-fit-stash.md rev 2, one Codex round folded - burst-start capture, Arc<RingSlot> aliasing, exact fit+inset+rotation identity, settle-hook beats Original-rebind/derive/CPU-want, external-bytes budget accounting, 4 core tests + 1 pb-core test). Owner smoke pending: park, F, F - second F instant, [sharp-diag] fit-stash re-present firing. FIX 1 SHIPPED 2026-07-19 (current-Original priority: the parked photo's own Original job is inserted directly after its display ladder in request_prefetch, ahead of neighbour previews/fulls and thumbs; neighbours/pin stay in the below-thumbs tail; order-pinned by the_current_photos_parked_original_outranks_the_neighbour_refill). FIX 2 (geometry-pair Fit stash) OWNER-APPROVED in direction, pending its own plan + Codex round: retain the previous geometry's presented Fit for the current photo, keyed by EXACT (item, content_gen, fit box) identity, budget-accounted, first-evicted; ~one Fit texture (~28-66MB) vs the multi-second re-decode; also the only possible instant path for derive-ineligible (ICC mode-1/RAW) photos. Owner note: does not need to cover novel resize sizes - the two-state fullscreen toggle is the common case.
Owner repro 2026-07-19 (engagement shoot, 36MP sRGB baseline JPEGs - file probe ruled out RAW/ICC-mode-1/progressive/size; thumbnail strip CLOSED): parked on a photo late in a 279-item folder, every F re-decodes visibly until 'way after the pie', and re-toggling mid-decode restarts the visible reload. Two mechanisms, confirmed by code reading:
(A) THE PIE MEASURES THE WRONG CONTRACT + THE ORIGINAL IS STARVED BY THE NEIGHBOUR REFILL. The pie clears on the Fit present, but instant toggles need the parked ORIGINAL, which is queued at the very bottom of the want list (below the ahead-ring fulls; below thumbs too, but the strip was closed here). Every F correctly kills all neighbour Fits and re-queues DOZENS of 36MP fit decodes above the Original, so repeated toggling keeps it perpetually at the back (~10s+ of queue at 36MP). FIX 1 (small, surgical): rank the CURRENT photo's parked Original directly after the current photo's own display ladder - above neighbour previews/fulls and thumbs. Bounded cost: exactly one decode job; parked = F/zoom is the next likely action (prime directive), its prerequisite must not queue behind 30 neighbours. The owner's below-thumbs calibration was about 'a few big originals' (the whole tier) starving visible thumbnails - promoting ONE job does not reopen that.
(B) THE ONE-DEEP HELD STASH ALWAYS MISSES A TWO-STATE OSCILLATION. On each geometry change the presented texture escapes into the single renderer 'held' fallback and every other Fit is freed; F is a two-point oscillation, so the texture you toggle BACK to was freed one toggle ago - 'I literally just had these pixels' re-decodes from scratch. FIX 2 (the owner's idea): a geometry-PAIR stash - retain the previous geometry's presented Fit texture for the current photo (keyed by item + fit box / epoch parity), so toggle-back is a pure rebind from the FIRST F, zero decode, before any Original exists. NOTE: this is also the ONLY possible instant-toggle path for derive-ineligible photos (ICC mode-1, RAW - derive_fit refuses them forever), so it is not just a race-window patch. Design care: keep it renderer+ring coherent (the #119 validity/#109.4 fail-loud discipline - a stashed texture must carry its fit identity so present can match exactly, never trust 'same epoch parity'); the stash is RAM/VRAM-only session state (privacy posture unchanged).
Sequencing: Fix 1 first (minutes, kills most of the felt pain: pie + ~one decode arms the derive path); Fix 2 second (design-review worthy, touches ring identity). Verify: park on _DE25786-class photo, F immediately and repeatedly - first toggle may decode once; toggle-back must be instant from then on, pie or no pie.

tasks.title: Zoom magnifies the fit-sized texture instead of raising resolution (rep selection is mode-derived, should be resolution-derived)
tasks.description:
OWNER BUG REPORT 2026-07-19: "zooming in only stretches the currently displayed texture but does not actually increase the resolution displayed." CONFIRMED by code reading (agent trace, no runtime repro yet).

EVIDENCE. Zoom is a pure vertex transform: zoom_step (app_core_impl.rs:2180) / zoom_about_cursor (:3825) / the hold-to-zoom ramp (:11392) all mutate view.zoom -> push_view (:8630) -> Renderer::set_view (pb-render/src/gpu.rs:3444), which ONLY rewrites the 4-vertex quad. UVs are always the full 0.0..1.0 (view.rs:48); view.rs:7 states the intent outright ('rotation/zoom/pan are perf-neutral transforms with no re-decode').

ROOT CAUSE. display_kind() (app_core_impl.rs:6666) and decode_fit() (:6628) pick the rep from view.mode ALONE - view.zoom is never consulted:
    match self.view.mode { Fit => self.fit, Fill | Original => None }
So in Fit mode the resident texture is fit-box-sized and zoom cannot reach the ring's Original slot, even when a full-res Original IS already resident (the parked tier, :6386, radius from full_res_radius() :6928). Mode is being used as a PROXY for 'how many source pixels does the screen need', and zoom is exactly the input that breaks the proxy. The correct predicate is resolution-derived, not mode-derived.

IMPACT. 24MP photo, 3840x2160 viewport, Fit mode, zoom to 300%: you are sampling ~1280x720 texels of the ~3840x2160 fit texture, magnified with a plain bilinear mag_filter (gpu.rs:3133; no anisotropy, no lod_clamp) - roughly 1/9 the detail the source could supply. MAX_ZOOM is 32 (view.rs:60), so it degrades much further. Fit-rep textures are also mip_level_count: 1 (only the Original gets mips, gpu.rs:1863/1913), so zoom-OUT in Fit mode is unfiltered minification too.

NO SETTLE HOOK EXISTS. The 180ms RESIZE_SETTLE debounce (engine.rs:143, armed at app_core_impl.rs:1506, drained :1925) is gated on a real fit-box change (:1435). No zoom path touches resize_settle_at, fit, epoch, invalidate_geometry, request_prefetch, or content_gen. Nothing is requested on zoom-stop because there is no zoom-stop.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG. set_scale_mode sets view.zoom = 1.0 (:5479), so pressing 0 / 1:1 masks it - in Original/Fill mode decode_fit() returns None, the full-res mipped texture is bound, and zoom magnifies real source pixels. That is currently the ONLY way to see native detail.

SCOPE, CORRECTED BY THE OWNER 2026-07-19: the assistant first read the comment at :6386-6392 ('a Fit<->1:1 toggle / zoom on those photos is an instant rebind') as an unimplemented CLAIM. The owner - who wrote it - clarified that 'zoom' there means the Fit<->1:1 MODE TOGGLE, not the smooth zoom. The comment is accurate and needs no fix, and this was never a regression from intended behavior; it is an unimplemented capability. That sharpens the bug rather than shrinking it:
  - Fit<->1:1 toggle: ALREADY CORRECT (set_scale_mode flips display_kind to Original and rebinds the resident full-res texture).
  - Smooth zoom in FIT mode (+/-, pinch, Ctrl+scroll, hold-to-zoom): THE GAP. Never flips the rep, so it magnifies the fit texture.
  - Smooth zoom in 1:1/Fill mode: already correct - the Original is bound, and past 100% it is correctly showing all the data that exists.
So the fix reduces to: make smooth zoom do what the 1:1 toggle already does. The machinery is built, shipped and proven (#106.7); only the trigger is missing - which lowers the risk profile considerably.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER (affects priority): which was actually observed - soft pixels while in Fit after a pinch/+ zoom (this bug), or softness while in 1:1 (a different problem, possibly not a bug at all)?

PROPOSED APPROACH (assistant recommendation, NOT owner-approved - wants a plan + Codex round before implementation). Three rungs of the existing cancellable refinement ladder:

RUNG 0 (the ballgame; instant, zero decode): make rep selection resolution-derived so that once zoom would magnify past the fit texture's native detail, display_kind() binds the RESIDENT Original instead of Fit. For any parked photo inside full_res_radius this is a pure rebind - exactly the 'never repeat likely work' corollary. Geometry should fall out for free rather than needing a stash: base_scale is computed from image_size(), which returns the BOUND TEXTURE's dims (gpu.rs:3669, screen_and_image at :11347), so base_scale * zoom * tex_size is identical either side of the swap and the image must not jump. VERIFY THAT CLAIM FIRST - it is the load-bearing assumption and it was reasoned, not measured. Also fixes zoom-out (the Original is mipped).

RUNG 1 (instant, no decode): while no better pixels exist, stop magnifying with bilinear. A Catmull-Rom / Lanczos magnification path costs nothing per frame and the GPU-Lanczos machinery (#110) plus pb-render's ab_report A/B/X harness already exist to pick the kernel on evidence rather than taste.

RUNG 2 (settle, cancellable; SEPARATE TASK once 0+1 are measured): for when the Original is NOT resident - full_res_radius 0, big RAW, outside the ring - request an ROI decode on zoom-stop, reusing the resize_settle_at debounce pattern, cancelled by any further zoom/pan/nav. The correct decode-to-purpose answer is NOT 'decode the full original': it is decode ONLY THE VISIBLE RECT at display resolution, which is bounded work regardless of zoom depth or source megapixels (a 300% view of a 24MP file is a ~1/9 crop at viewport res - CHEAPER than the fit decode was). KNOWN OBSTACLE: decode-to-purpose today means FitBox, i.e. a SCALE not a CROP. Adding an ROI rect is real work and backend support is uneven - JPEG DCT-block cropping is cheap, most other backends mean decode-full-then-crop, which defeats the purpose for precisely the big files that need it most. Ship 0+1 first and measure; rung 2 may only matter at radius 0.

SCOPE NOTE: the macOS host was not audited for a separate zoom implementation. The Renderer trait seam (pb-render/src/lib.rs:229) suggests it shares set_view, but that is unverified - check pb-mac-ffi / mac/ before assuming the fix is cross-platform by construction.

PRIME DIRECTIVE FRAMING: parked zoom is a parked interaction, so it owes both budgets - interaction -> photon <= one refresh (rung 0 is a rebind, so it clears trivially) AND time-to-max-quality after parking (today: never, at any zoom > 1 in Fit mode).

Audit finding #1 remediation (a), and the audit's #1 recommended action - never filed as a task, which is likely why it is the one recommendation that did not happen while #109/#119/#121 all did. Plan: .taskmaster/plans/125-split-app-core-impl.md.

WHY NOW. app_core_impl.rs went 15,898 -> 20,546 lines between 2026-07-18 (8b5dc30b, the audit's own baseline) and 2026-07-19, and 20,932 at 5f3b4429: +5,034 lines / +32% in about a day, in the very file the audit had just named its top debt. Re-measured at HEAD: 20,932 lines (11,963 production + 8,970 tests), 349 production methods in essentially one flat impl AppCore. Next-largest file in the repo is gpu.rs at 7,127, so this is ~2.9x the runner-up. The audit's stated figures (16,013 / 323 methods / mod tests at 10011) are all now stale in the same direction - its freshness caveat predicted exactly this.

COST, OBSERVED (not theoretical) during task #124: two full Codex review runs returned NOTHING because both exhausted their budget exploring the file - a review was only obtained by hand-extracting excerpts into the prompt; a patch landed in the WRONG function first (rebuild_playlist vs rebuild_ring, plausible-looking neighbours in a 349-entry list); and 'what else touches this?' needs a repo-wide grep because it cannot be answered by reading a file.

SCOPE GATE - THE MOST IMPORTANT PART. This is remediation (a) ONLY: move methods into concern-scoped `impl AppCore` blocks in new files. NOT (b) finishing the NS0 inversion (AppCore owns orchestration, mirror flags get one owner), and NOT (c) ending the ~165-pub-field sprawl. No field moves, no signature changes, no visibility changes, no AppCore struct changes, no call-site edits, NO RENAMES. If a method looks wrong while being moved, note it and move it unchanged. Bundling (a) with (b) is the main way this goes wrong: it converts a provably-safe file move into a behavioral refactor and destroys the safety property below.

THE SAFETY PROPERTY. Rust allows multiple `impl AppCore` blocks across files in one crate, so every method moves with zero call-site/type/visibility change. That makes the refactor PROVABLY behavior-preserving rather than merely tested: extract every fn body from the crate, normalize (sort by name, drop file boundaries and use-lines), hash, and require before == after for every commit. A non-empty body diff is a bug, not a judgement call. cargo test (830 in pb-app-core) is the backstop, not the proof - a passing suite would not catch a silently dropped method that nothing covers.

CLUSTERS (measured at HEAD, auto-clustered by method name, LOC each would take along): video/audio/playback/poster/subtitle 96 fns/2,882 LOC; residency/decode/present/ring 44/2,388 (THE HOT ENGINE - moves last or not at all); unassigned-needs-triage 59/1,878; lifecycle/dispatch 10/1,101 (tick alone is 487); panels/overlay/hud 40/891; tree/fs/nav 38/856; file ops/undo 15/581; view/geometry 22/568; scan/describe/text 13/395; settings/keymap 5/185; archive/door 7/129. The eight LEAF clusters are ~6,487 LOC ~= 54% of production and their tests travel with them, so extracting only the leaves takes the file to roughly 6-8k WITHOUT touching the hot path once.

SEQUENCING: leaf-first, one cluster per commit - prefs (smallest, a full rehearsal of the process incl. the verifier) -> archive/scan/view -> files/tree/panels -> video (the big win, after the process is proven six times) -> STOP AND REASSESS. Splitting the residency engine is a separate and more debatable question (genuinely coupled, and the hot path); do not pre-commit to it. tick (487 lines) and dispatch_action are NOT decomposed here - cutting them up is a behavior risk to per-frame ordering, file separately if wanted.

TOP RISK IS MERGE CONFLICTS, NOT CORRECTNESS: the owner edits this tree concurrently and this is the repo's #1 churn file. Land each step in its own commit the same day, confirm nothing is mid-flight in a cluster before moving it, stage explicit paths (never add -A). A conflict is unusually safe to resolve here precisely because the body diff mechanically proves the resolution preserved every method.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX (so the task is not oversold): AppCore still has ~165 pub fields and any method in any new file can still touch any of them, so the blast radius is unchanged IN PRINCIPLE - only navigability, review size and merge-conflict surface improve.
